newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa diesel price set to fall 4 cts/ltr in Apr.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa diesel price set to fall 4 cts/ltr in Apr.

text.p: South African diesel prices are set to be cut by a further four cents a litre from April 2, bringing the reduction in the price to nearly 10 percent in two months.
According to latest Central Energy Fund (CEF) data, there was an over-recovery of 4.238 cents a litre on the diesel price between February 26 and March 25.
The data also showed, however, that petrol recorded an under-recovery of 1.937 cents a litre, which pointed to a rise in the retail price of between one and two cents a litre.

A CEF spokeswoman said the diesel over-recovery would probably result in a four-cent reduction, bringing the retail price to 200 cents a litre -- a 9.3 percent reduction on the price in February, following a 19-cent price cut on March 5.
EW Balderson economist Mike Schussler put the likely cut in the diesel price down to statistical factors and noted that the price was set to rise again from May.
"Because of the huge drop last month and another drop this month, it means that the over-recovery is too strong," he said.
This would result in an under-recovery taking effect from May and thus prices would have to rise, he said.
Schussler that while retail petrol prices were likely to rise by between one and two cents in April, they could be reduced in the months ahead following a decline in international oil prices.
May Brent crude oil has fallen from a peak of $20.84 a barrel on March 19 to $19.64 on Wednesday, but is up from $18.70 at the beginning of the month.
Schussler said international oil prices had been depressed by the fact that Iraqi oil sales had come on stream -- a factor which could further weigh on prices in the months ahead.
"Petrol has an under-recovery and will continue to have a slight under-recovery for most of next month because oil price drops take a while to work through the system," Schussler said.

"But the lower oil price means that at the end of next month the petrol price will start showing an over-recovery, bringing down the average for next month and which could result in a petrol price cut," he said.
The pump price of petrol currently stands at 219 cents a litre.
